You are Reservoir engineer I: subsurface and wells. Design the doublet `d0` of the stored design `design/start` (gemini class HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant, one doublet). Read the handbook chapters 3 and 4 (knowledge/handbook-design.md, sections '3 Wells' and '4 ...') and skill evaluating-a-module.

CASE VALUES (from read_case, case hackathon_2026): site.ground.surface_temperature 12 degC; site.ground.gradient 30 K/km; site.reservoir.reference_depth 2500 m; site.reservoir.pressure 250 barg; site.reservoir.thickness 100 m; site.reservoir.permeability 200 mD; site.fluid.density 1030 kg/m3; site.fluid.viscosity 0.4 mPa.s; site.fluid.gas_liquid_ratio 0.8 Nm3/m3; site.fluid.sand_concentration 20 mg/l; site.fluid.dissolved_gas CH4 0.8, CO2 0.2.

INTERFACE VALUES I (lead) settled: doublet depth 2500 m (the case's reference depth); reservoir temperature at that depth = 87 degC (calculation Cd5099b: 12 degC + 30 K/km x 2500 m); reservoir pressure 250 barg from the case. Requirement brine_cooling_limit: each doublet cools brine at most 40 K while running, so the brine may leave the surface plant no colder than 47 degC. Requirement production_flow_range: each doublet 50-300 m3/h while running. Requirement pump_efficiency = 0.7 exactly. Requirement full_reinjection: reinjection ratio 1.0. Requirement running_time_limit: at most 330 d per doublet.

YOUR PATHS (all under params.d0, gemini's issue text in brackets):
- params.d0.depth [missing; with it the doublet takes its reservoir temperature and pressure from the case]
- params.d0.drainage_radius [Radius of the drainage area around each well, m]
- params.d0.roughness [Absolute roughness of the inner wall of both vertical wells, m]
- params.d0.reservoir.pressure [Static reservoir pressure, Pa], .temperature [Undisturbed reservoir temperature, K], .permeability [m2], .aquifer_thickness [m], .drainage_radius [m], .top_depth [m], .skin [-], .wellbore_radius [m]
- params.d0.well.section_length [m], .section_inclination [rad], .section_diameter [m], .section_roughness [m], .friction_correlation, .two_phase_friction_correlation, .correction_factors, .soil_temperature [K], .heat_transfer_coefficient [W/m2/K], .segment
- params.d0.riser.* (same list as well.*)
- params.d0.injector.* (same list as well.*)
- params.d0.sink.pressure [Pa], .temperature [K], .permeability [m2], .aquifer_thickness [m], .drainage_radius [m], .top_depth [m], .skin [-], .wellbore_radius [m]
- params.d0.esp.stage_count [-], .head_coefficients, .power_coefficients, .pump_type, .setting_depth [m], .motor_efficiency [-], .minimum_flow [m3/s], .maximum_flow [m3/s], .best_efficiency_flow [m3/s], .correction_factors, .drift_threshold [-]
- params.d0.riser.esp_depth if gemini asks for it (the pump depth is yours, never mine).

RULES: the ESP is yours. If no source gives a pump curve, use pump_type "unspecified" with no head/power coefficients (as gemini's reference plant does): the doublet then derives them from its complete design values and the case's pump efficiency 0.7. Never invent a catalogue curve. Every value needs a source (case path, or an equipment assumption with a one-line reason). Do not touch any path outside params.d0. Return changes as [{path, value, source, reason}] with values as {"value", "unit"} where dimensional, plus any evaluations you need from gemini and any couplings you see.

INTERFACE VALUES I (lead) settled: one doublet at 2500 m, brine produced at 87 degC (calculation Cd5099b), reservoir pressure 250 barg; brine flow will be in the case's 50-300 m3/h band per doublet; the degasser's gas goes to gas_makeup -> peak_boiler fuel, surplus to flare; the peak boiler burns gas.

YOUR PATHS (gemini's issue text in brackets):
- params.degasser.nominal_pressure_drop [Pressure drop across the vessel at the nominal flow, Pa], .separation_efficiency [Share of the inlet free gas that leaves through the gas outlet, -]
- params.filters.hot.nominal_pressure_drop [Pa], .nominal_mass_flow [kg/s]
- params.filters.cold.nominal_pressure_drop [Pa], .nominal_mass_flow [kg/s]

RULES: every value needs a source (case path, or an equipment assumption with a one-line reason). Do not touch any path outside your group (no d0.*, no heat_pump/boiler/chiller). Return changes as [{path, value, source, reason}] with values as {"value", "unit"} where dimensional, plus any evaluations you need from gemini and any couplings you see.

You are Energy systems engineer I: heating. Design the heating side of the stored design `design/start` (gemini class HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant). Read handbook chapters 6, 8.3 and 9 (knowledge/handbook-design.md) and skill evaluating-a-module.

CASE VALUES: heating demand from data/demand.csv, peak 30 MW, annual energy 111667.68 MWh, mean 12.75 MW; heating supply 100 degC, return 60 degC, return pressure 6 bar. Brine from the doublet: 87 degC at 2500 m (calculation Cd5099b), reservoir pressure 250 barg. Requirement brine_cooling_limit: brine may leave the surface plant no colder than 47 degC (40 K cap). Requirement heat_delivered: unmet share of heating supply at most 0.01. Requirement pump_efficiency 0.7.

PLANT TEXT of your modules (from the class file): heat_exchanger (HeatExchanger) hot_in from filters.hot.fluid_out, hot_out to heat_pump.source_in, cold_in from heating_return_pipe.fluid_out, cold_out to heat_pump.sink_in; heat_pump (HeatPump) source_in from heat_exchanger.hot_out, source_out to filters.cold.fluid_in, sink_in from heat_exchanger.cold_out, sink_out to peak_boiler.fluid_in, power_in from electricity_grid; peak_boiler (Boiler) fluid_in from heat_pump.sink_out, fluid_out to heating_supply_pipe.fluid_in, fuel_in from gas_makeup.fuel_out, flue_out to atmosphere; heating_supply_pipe and heating_return_pipe (Pipe) to/from heating_consumer (HeatingGrid, supply 100 degC / return 60 degC from the case).

YOUR PATHS (gemini's issue text in brackets):
- params.heat_exchanger.thermal_conductance [UA, W/K], .arrangement [Flow arrangement of the two streams], .hot_nominal_pressure_drop [Pa], .cold_nominal_pressure_drop [Pa], .hot_nominal_mass_flow [kg/s], .cold_nominal_mass_flow [kg/s]
- params.heat_pump.mode [heating or cooling], .capacity [W], .cop_model [Carnot fraction or Lorenz], .carnot_fraction [-], .lorenz_fraction [-], .minimum_temperature_lift [K]
- params.peak_boiler.capacity [W], .efficiency [-]
- params.heating_supply_pipe.length [m], .inner_diameter [m], .roughness [m], .elevation_change [m], .heat_transfer_coefficient [W/m2/K]
- params.heating_return_pipe.* (same list)

RULES: the heat pump is in heating mode on the brine; its source outlet must not go below 47 degC (set minimum_source_outlet_temperature if the module has it, else keep the duty such that the brine stays above 47 degC). The peak boiler covers the peak with the doublets off (params.backup = peak, my decision). Every value needs a source (case path, or an equipment assumption with a one-line reason). Do not touch d0.*, the degasser/filters/flare, or the cooling modules. Return changes as [{path, value, source, reason}] with values as {"value", "unit"} where dimensional, plus any evaluations you need from gemini and any couplings you see.

You are Energy systems engineer II: cooling. Design the cooling side of the stored design `design/start` (gemini class HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant). Read handbook chapter 7 (knowledge/handbook-design.md) and skill evaluating-a-module.

CASE VALUES: cooling demand from data/demand.csv, peak 10 MW, mean 2.71 MW; cooling supply 20 degC, return 25 degC, return pressure 4 bar; site.air.temperature 10 degC, site.air.pressure 101325 Pa; utilities.electricity.co2_intensity 300 g/kWh. Requirement cold_delivered: unmet share of cooling supply at most 0.01.

PLANT TEXT of your modules (from the class file): compression_chiller (HeatPump) source_in from cooling_return_pipe.fluid_out, source_out to cooling_supply_pipe.fluid_in, sink_out to compression_cooler.fluid_in, sink_in from compression_cooler.fluid_out, power_in from electricity_grid; compression_cooler (Cooler) fluid_in from compression_chiller.sink_out, fluid_out to compression_chiller.sink_in, air_in from atmosphere.air_out, air_out to atmosphere.air_in, power_in from electricity_grid; cooling_supply_pipe and cooling_return_pipe (Pipe) to/from cooling_consumer (CoolingGrid, supply 20 degC / return 25 degC from the case).

YOUR PATHS (gemini's issue text in brackets):
- params.compression_chiller.mode [heating or cooling], .capacity [W], .cop_model [Carnot fraction or Lorenz], .carnot_fraction [-], .lorenz_fraction [-], .minimum_temperature_lift [K]
- params.compression_cooler.cooler_type [dry air cooler or wet (evaporative) cooler], .capacity [W], .approach [K], .specific_fan_power [-]
- params.cooling_supply_pipe.length [m], .inner_diameter [m], .roughness [m], .elevation_change [m], .heat_transfer_coefficient [W/m2/K]
- params.cooling_return_pipe.* (same list)

RULES: the chiller is an electric compression chiller in cooling mode rejecting to the air cooler. Every value needs a source (case path, or an equipment assumption with a one-line reason). Do not touch d0.*, the treatment modules, or the heating modules. Return changes as [{path, value, source, reason}] with values as {"value", "unit"} where dimensional, plus any evaluations you need from gemini and any couplings you see.

A large result does not come back whole. You get a summary and a `reference` to the stored data.

- A summary gives the minimum, maximum and mean and the unit of each field. It is enough for most
  answers, so start there.
- When you need the values themselves, call `read_result(reference, path, field, start, end)`. `path`
  is the module path, `field` the field name, and `start` and `end` are ISO times of the case. Leave
  them out for the whole series, and prefer a short window.
- A question about a stored result is one `read_result` call, never code:
  - the peak or the lowest value and its day, the days or steps a value is not zero: the series
    of that field, `read_result(reference, path, field)`; its `summary` gives `max` and `min`
    with their `time`, `mean`, `active_steps`, `active_days`, `first_active` and `last_active`.
    Example: the peak heat delivered and its day is the summary's `max` of the heat field.
  - how many days a module ran (a doublet's pump, a boiler) and the energy it used:
    `read_result(reference, path)`; its `operation` gives `operating_days` and
    `operating_steps` (days with flow) of `steps`, and `energy_whole_run` per energy output in
    MWh. A module without an energy output (a heat exchanger) has no `energy_whole_run`: that
    does not mean it was unused; its `operating_days` and its duty series say how it ran.
  - energies of the whole plant: `check_results` `metrics` (`heat_delivered`, `cold_delivered`,
    `boiler_heat`, `electricity_bought`, `gas_bought`); the heat not from the boiler is
    `heat_delivered` minus `boiler_heat`, one `calculate` call.
  - whether each requirement passes, with its number: `check_results` `requirements`; each entry
    has `name`, `passed`, `value` (the worst value of the run: brine cooling in K, running days
    in d, reinjection ratio, flow), `limit`, `unit_path` (which doublet or module) and
    `worst_step` (its day). Quote `value` against `limit` for every requirement; never write that
    a requirement "rests on the verdict" when its entry has a value.
  - a doublet's production flow against its range: the series `<doublet>.reservoir.liquid_flow`
    (the liquid at brine density, what the requirement judges). The pump's
    `fluid_in.volume_flow` also counts the free gas at the intake pressure, so it reads higher
    (341 m3/h for 300 m3/h of liquid) and is no flow limit.
  Use `run_python` only for what none of these gives, and never to sum a power series into an
  energy: the energies come from gemini in MWh.
- A wrong `path` or `field` is an error result that lists what exists, so read it and try again.
- Keep the reference of a result you record with `update_state`, so that it can be read again later.
- `check_results` of a result returns `feasible` (gemini's verdict), `reasons` (each with a `kind`
  of `requirement`, `failed_step`, `numerical` or `bound`, a `name` and a `message`), the
  `requirements` it judged and the `failures`. Report the reasons as they are; a result with a
  failed step is not feasible, whatever its totals say.
- Values come in display units (MW, MWh, degC, Pa, EUR/MWh); report each with its unit.

## The tools

### `check_results`

Check stored results against the case they ran on: gemini's verdict and report.

Returns `{feasible, reasons, requirements, failures, metrics}`, gemini's, in display units.
`feasible` is `gm.evaluate.verdict`, the one rule: true when nothing is wrong. `reasons`
says what is, each with a `kind` (`requirement`, `failed_step`, `numerical` or
`bound`), a `name` and a `message`. `requirements` is one check per unit of each
requirement of the case and per service supply temperature, `failures` the failed and skipped
steps by module and code, and `metrics` the energies, capacities, costs and CO2. A limit is a
requirement of the case: set it with `set_case`.

### `read_result`

Return one series of a stored run, or a summary of the run or of one module path.

`reference` is what simulate returned. With `path` and `field` it returns the series
`{time, value, unit, summary}`, `summary` being `{steps, unit, max: {value, unit, time}, min:
{value, unit, time}, mean, active_steps, active_days, first_active, last_active}` (active: not

Return a result that was stored by reference, whole or one part of it.

`reference` is the `result-...` (or `output-...`) key of a result that came back as a
reference and an outline. `path` is dotted keys and list indexes into it, such as

A large result does not come back whole. You get a summary and a `reference` to the stored data.

- A summary gives the minimum, maximum and mean and the unit of each field. It is enough for most
  answers, so start there.
- When you need the values themselves, call `read_result(reference, path, field, start, end)`. `path`
  is the module path, `field` the field name, and `start` and `end` are ISO times of the case. Leave
  them out for the whole series, and prefer a short window.
- A question about a stored result is one `read_result` call, never code:
  - the peak or the lowest value and its day, the days or steps a value is not zero: the series
    of that field, `read_result(reference, path, field)`; its `summary` gives `max` and `min`
    with their `time`, `mean`, `active_steps`, `active_days`, `first_active` and `last_active`.
    Example: the peak heat delivered and its day is the summary's `max` of the heat field.
  - how many days a module ran (a doublet's pump, a boiler) and the energy it used:
    `read_result(reference, path)`; its `operation` gives `operating_days` and
    `operating_steps` (days with flow) of `steps`, and `energy_whole_run` per energy output in
    MWh. A module without an energy output (a heat exchanger) has no `energy_whole_run`: that
    does not mean it was unused; its `operating_days` and its duty series say how it ran.
  - energies of the whole plant: `check_results` `metrics` (`heat_delivered`, `cold_delivered`,
    `boiler_heat`, `electricity_bought`, `gas_bought`); the heat not from the boiler is
    `heat_delivered` minus `boiler_heat`, one `calculate` call.
  - whether each requirement passes, with its number: `check_results` `requirements`; each entry
    has `name`, `passed`, `value` (the worst value of the run: brine cooling in K, running days
    in d, reinjection ratio, flow), `limit`, `unit_path` (which doublet or module) and
    `worst_step` (its day). Quote `value` against `limit` for every requirement; never write that
    a requirement "rests on the verdict" when its entry has a value.
  - a doublet's production flow against its range: the series `<doublet>.reservoir.liquid_flow`
    (the liquid at brine density, what the requirement judges). The pump's
    `fluid_in.volume_flow` also counts the free gas at the intake pressure, so it reads higher
    (341 m3/h for 300 m3/h of liquid) and is no flow limit.
  Use `run_python` only for what none of these gives, and never to sum a power series into an
  energy: the energies come from gemini in MWh.
- A wrong `path` or `field` is an error result that lists what exists, so read it and try again.
- Keep the reference of a result you record with `update_state`, so that it can be read again later.
- `check_results` of a result returns `feasible` (gemini's verdict), `reasons` (each with a `kind`
  of `requirement`, `failed_step`, `numerical` or `bound`, a `name` and a `message`), the
  `requirements` it judged and the `failures`. Report the reasons as they are; a result with a
  failed step is not feasible, whatever its totals say.
- Values come in display units (MW, MWh, degC, Pa, EUR/MWh); report each with its unit.

## The tools

### `check_results`

Check stored results against the case they ran on: gemini's verdict and report.

Returns `{feasible, reasons, requirements, failures, metrics}`, gemini's, in display units.
`feasible` is `gm.evaluate.verdict`, the one rule: true when nothing is wrong. `reasons`
says what is, each with a `kind` (`requirement`, `failed_step`, `numerical` or
`bound`), a `name` and a `message`. `requirements` is one check per unit of each
requirement of the case and per service supply temperature, `failures` the failed and skipped
steps by module and code, and `metrics` the energies, capacities, costs and CO2. A limit is a
requirement of the case: set it with `set_case`.

### `read_result`

Return one series of a stored run, or a summary of the run or of one module path.

`reference` is what simulate returned. With `path` and `field` it returns the series
`{time, value, unit, summary}`, `summary` being `{steps, unit, max: {value, unit, time}, min:
{value, unit, time}, mean, active_steps, active_days, first_active, last_active}` (active: not
zero; days are UTC calendar days); `start` and `end` are ISO 8601 times, both inclusive. With
only `path` it returns `{<path>: {field: {min, max, mean}}, operation: {steps, operating_steps,
operating_days, energy_whole_run}}`, and with neither min, max and mean of every module of the
whole run. Power is in MW, temperature in degC, pressure in bar, flows in m3/h or kg/s.

### `read_stored`

Return a result that was stored by reference, whole or one part of it.

`reference` is the `result-...` (or `output-...`) key of a result that came back as a
reference and an outline. `path` is dotted keys and list indexes into it, such as
`capabilities.HeatingPlant` (`/` reads as `.`). A part too long to show whole comes
back as its keys (or its length) and an outline, with the path to read deeper.
